evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-01"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z", so the date is stored as a calendar date at midnight UTC. POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. Both worked.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/4 with {"dueDate":"2026-10-02"} set the date (200). PATCH {"title":"none2"} kept the date. PATCH {"dueDate":null} cleared it (dueDate null). PATCH with a new date set it again.
evidence.AC3: Returned 400 for these dueDate values on POST: "2026-02-30", "10/01/2026", "2026-13-01", "abc" and "2026-10-01T10:00:00". PATCH with "2026-02-30" also returned 400. However, POST with a numeric dueDate (20261001) returned 201 and silently stored dueDate null instead of rejecting it. Not every invalid-format value is rejected.
evidence.AC4: Today is 2026-10-14. I created todos due 2026-10-01 (not done), 2026-12-01, 2026-10-14 (today), none, and 2026-09-01 (then marked done). GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the 2026-10-01 todo and the todo whose date I later set to 2026-10-02. The future, today, no-date and done-past todos were excluded.
evidence.AC5: The list page at / showed each todo's due date: 01.10.2026, 01.12.2026, 14.10.2026, 02.10.2026 and 01.09.2026. The todo with no due date showed none.
evidence.AC6: In the page snapshot, 'überfällig' appeared only on the two overdue todos (01.10.2026 and 02.10.2026). The future, today, done-past and no-date todos had no marker.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled 'nur überfällige'. After I clicked it, the list showed only the two overdue todos (past and none2).
